name: Inferior vena cava
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Formed by the union of the two common iliac veins at L5; drains into the right atrium. Hepatic veins (draining the liver directly into the IVC just below the diaphragm) are visceral detail outside NMSK scope.

name: Common iliac vein (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Formed by union of external_iliac_v_r (modeled as the root of data/vascular/lower_limb_venous.json) and internal_iliac_v_r.

name: Common iliac vein (left)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Longer than the right and crosses the midline to reach the IVC, passing beneath the right common iliac artery -- the anatomical basis of May-Thurner compression syndrome.

name: Renal vein (right)
supplies_or_drains: kidney (visceral organ, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Renal vein (left)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Longer than the right, crossing the midline anterior to the aorta (potential 'nutcracker' compression point between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery).

name: Gonadal vein (right)
supplies_or_drains: gonad (visceral organ, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Right gonadal vein drains directly into the IVC at an oblique angle.

name: Gonadal vein (left)
supplies_or_drains: gonad (visceral organ, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein rather than the IVC directly -- a well-documented right/left asymmetry, and the anatomical basis for left-sided predominance of varicocele.

name: Ascending lumbar vein (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Longitudinal channel connecting the lumbar veins to the azygos system -- the main lumbar-to-thoracic venous continuity, and (with the azygos/hemiazygos system as a whole) a clinically important collateral pathway when the IVC is obstructed.

name: Azygos vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Right-sided vessel ascending in the posterior mediastinum, arching over the right main bronchus to drain into the superior vena cava (SVC/heart-side termination is Stage 3/mediastinal territory, not modeled here). Receives the right posterior intercostal veins, the right subcostal vein, and the hemiazygos/accessory hemiazygos systems.

name: Superior vena cava
supplies_or_drains: venous return from the head, neck, upper limbs and thoracic wall
notes: Formed behind the right first costal cartilage by the union of the two brachiocephalic veins. Obstruction produces SVC syndrome -- facial and upper limb swelling, distended neck veins, collateral chest wall veins -- most often from bronchogenic carcinoma or indwelling catheter thrombus.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Brachiocephalic (innominate) vein, right
supplies_or_drains: right internal jugular and subclavian venous return
notes: Short and nearly vertical, which is why right-sided central venous access offers the straighter path into the SVC and is generally preferred.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Brachiocephalic (innominate) vein, left
supplies_or_drains: left internal jugular and subclavian venous return
thoracic duct, which terminates near its junction with the left subclavian vein
notes: Crosses the midline behind the manubrium and is about twice the length of the right. That longer, more angled course makes left-sided central line placement more prone to malposition and to vessel wall erosion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
